title: Replace a blade in a quick-release holder and check it is retained
instruction: Replace the worn grey/red blade with the blue/white training blade. 1. Turn the orange collar lever toward the robot bases about 35 degrees (40-degree stop) and hold it. 2. Pull the worn blade straight out and put it in the green tray. 3. With the collar held, insert the blue blade straight, notched tang first and black edge down, until its shoulder stops at the holder nose. 4. Release the collar so the pin locks. 5. Grip the blue end block; open the other gripper and keep it at least 6 cm clear of the holder, collar and pin. Pull outward until the spring carriage extends at least 6 mm; hold for 0.5 s while the blade remains seated and locked, then relax. 6. Open both grippers and withdraw at least 6 cm from the lever and blades; leave everything still for 2 s. The complete evaluated numbered manual is instruction.txt.
context: Changing a blade in a twist-collar quick-release clamp: one hand keeps the spring-return collar turned while the other removes the old blade and seats the new one; a tug confirms the lock.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the two arm bases, y to the left, from the midpoint between the bases; heights above the table. A bench blade holder (grey, 2.4 x 6 x 3.2 cm) sits on a spring carriage on a rail at x 30 cm, its insertion axis along y at 7 cm height, nose face at y 2 cm, open toward -y. An orange collar at the nose turns about the axis (rest stop 0, 40 degrees travel, spring return) with a lever tab on top (tip 5 cm above the axis). A red spring-loaded locking pin in the holder drops into a notch in the blade tang; a cam peg on the collar lifts it when the collar turns. The worn training blade is installed: grey, red mark, 6 mm thick, 17 cm body (30 mm tall) plus 5 cm tang (16 mm tall, 10 mm notch in its top edge), black blunt lower edge, grip block (2 x 3 x 3 cm) at the far end, 60 g. The new blade is identical but blue with a white mark, lying parallel to the axis in a two-fork rack at x 40 cm. A green rest tray (9 x 22 cm inside, 2 cm walls) is at (20, -10) cm. Intended build materials: steel holder/carriage/rail, locking pin and springs; polymer collar/lever, blunt training blades with moulded end grips, rack and tray. The fixed rail is 5 x 12 x 2 cm, centred at (30, 4) cm, 1 cm high. The rack has two forks centred at x 40 cm and y -3/-12 cm: each base is 2 x 1.2 x 2.5 cm, topped by two 0.4 x 1.2 x 1.2 cm side posts with an 8 mm opening. Tray floor is 9.8 x 22.8 x 0.4 cm, walls 0.4 cm thick. Parts are original nominal training geometry with authored masses and contact coefficients.
scoring: Measured state only. 0.25: worn blade out of the holder and resting in the tray. 0.5: also the new blade seated (shoulder within -2.5..+1 mm of its seat, on the axis within 1.2 mm, within 8 degrees, notch up). 0.75: also locked (pin within 1 mm of its engaged stop, collar within 3 degrees of rest). 1.0 (trial ends): also a retention check passed (holder carriage extended 6 mm or more, about 1.2 N at 150 N/m including 0.3 N preload, for 0.5 s while seated and locked, one gripper 10-50% open with its TCP within 2 cm of the blue end block, and the other at least 80% open and its TCP 6 cm from the holder centre, collar lever and pin follower), then both grippers open and 6 cm away and all parts at rest for 2 s. Unlocking, unseating or invalid measurements invalidate the check. The installed start scores 0; non-finite states score 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: reinstall the worn blade, put the new blade back in its rack, empty the tray.
fidelity: Approximate rigid-body model: holder, collar, pin and blades are rigid boxes; the collar cam lifts the pin by contact. Springs are joint drives (collar 0.0025 N m/deg, pin 300 N/m, carriage 150 N/m) with travel stops; pin-holder and collar-holder contacts are off (bores not modelled). Blunt training inserts; no cutting, blade flex or wear. Tug grasp uses measured finger opening and TCP proximity, without contact-force sensing.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (1,200 steps, seed 0); scripted demo: 1.0 in both episodes, including reset repeat (625 steps each).
